correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the full theorem for each fixed 0<alpha<2, sigma,r>0 and -1<Lambda<1, with the symmetric stable characteristic exponent sigma^alpha |k|^alpha, actual post-jump location and one rate-r independent Poisson reset clock. The Lévy density c|z|^{-1-alpha} integrates to lambda across the exterior of (-1,1) after shift Lambda. On each reset excursion, decompose jumps at delta L. Large jumps have rate O_delta(L^-alpha); two or more before independent Exp(r) time cost O_delta(L^-2alpha). The compensated symmetric small jumps have quadratic variation 2c(delta L)^{2-alpha}/(2-alpha), and stopped Doob yields an O(delta^{2-alpha} epsilon^-2 L^-alpha) probability of macroscopic displacement. After excluding the O(epsilon L^-alpha) boundary landing band and controlling tails, the marked single-excursion success measure converges at rate L^-alpha to (c/r)|y-Lambda|^-1-alpha dy. In particular p_L~lambda/(rL^alpha). The factor e^{-s tau_L/L^alpha} changes the successful measure by at most O(L^-alpha sqrt(p_L)) =o(L^-alpha) since tau_L<R and E R²=2/r². The exact geometric renewal transform q_L(s,g)/(1-E[e^{-sR/L^alpha}1_{R<tau_L}]) has denominator (s+lambda)/(rL^alpha)+o(L^-alpha), yielding Exp(lambda)×Pi for all s≥0 and bounded continuous g. Integrating the exterior power law gives the stated side bias and conditional Pareto overshoots. All limiting integrations are finite because Lambda strictly interior and alpha>0; alpha<2 is needed for the small-jump variance cutoff. Independent code repeated 243 bounded constant, normalizer, tail, Laplace and finite-renewal checks; these are not substitutes for the analytic infinite-L proof. Excluded alpha=2, varying parameters and convergence-rate assertions.

value.rationale: The model, large-interval scale and mean exit-time problem are natural and already investigated. The complete two-coordinate weak limit gives the limiting exit sign, size of the terminal overshoot and independence of where a heavy-tailed search exits from how long it takes, quantities not implied by the previously published mean asymptotic. Exact asymmetric reset-point bias and conditional Pareto tail formulas are independently useful for stochastic search risk and first-exit mark questions. The value is a self-contained nontrivial marked rare-event refinement, without asserting a novel general regeneration method or a wider theorem.

final_claim: For every fixed 0<alpha<2, sigma,r>0 and Lambda in (-1,1), a symmetric alpha-stable Lévy flight reset to Lambda L by a rate-r Poisson clock has (T_L/L^alpha, X_{T_L}/L) converging weakly to an independent Exp(lambda_Lambda) clock and Pi_Lambda exit-location mark, with lambda=(c/alpha) [(1-Lambda)^(-alpha)+(1+Lambda)^(-alpha)] and Pi density (c/lambda)|y-Lambda|^(-1-alpha) on |y|>=1. The right-exit probability and conditional Pareto-type overshoot tails stated in RESULT.md follow. The claim excludes alpha=2 and joint moving-parameter limits.
